bib.title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
bib.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2023

question: Can an RNN formulation trainable in parallel like a transformer, with constant-memory inference, match transformer quality at billions of parameters?
hypothesis: A linear-attention variant (RWKV) can be run as a transformer for training and as an RNN for inference, matching similarly sized transformers at lower inference cost.
contributions: The introduction of RWKV, a novel architecture combining RNNs and Transformer advantages while mitigating their limitations.
Detailed experiments demonstrating RWKV's performance and efficiency on benchmark datasets for large-scale models.
The release of pretrained models, from 169 million to 14 billion parameters, trained on the Pile.

method.summary: RWKV replaces QK attention with a channel-wise time-decay WKV operator plus token shift and receptance gating, computed in parallel over time for training and as a recurrence with a fixed-size state for decoding. Six models from 169M to 14B were pretrained for one epoch (330B tokens) on the Pile and compared FLOP-matched with Pythia, OPT and BLOOM; inference time and memory were benchmarked against several transformer families.
method.task: autoregressive language-model pretraining; zero-shot NLP benchmarks; long-context and inference-cost evaluation

models.name: RWKV-4-Raven-14B

other.finetune data: public instruction sets named in Ethics Statement (Alpaca, Code Alpaca, Guanaco, GPT4All, ShareGPT, BELLE etc.); no recipe given

training.objective: next-token cross-entropy plus PaLM auxiliary loss (pushes softmax normalizer toward zero)
training.lr_schedule: constant for warmup mini-epochs, then exponential decay to End LR (1e-5; 7e-6 for 14B) at the end of the Pile
training.warmup: constant LR at Init LR for 361/411/443/451/465/544 mini-epochs (169M..14B); mini-epoch = 40320 samples
training.batch_size: dynamically switched between 128 or 256 sequences of 1024 tokens
training.steps: 8043 mini-epochs for one pass over the Pile
training.compute: Fig 4 compute axis in exaFLOP; FLOP per token = 2(2VD+13D^2L) forward, 6(2VD+13D^2L) with backward; GPU hours not stated (compute provided by StabilityAI)

other.small init embedding: embedding U(+-1e-4) then extra LayerNorm; ablation batch size 400
other.custom init: zeros for most weights, no linear biases (Appendix E)
other.context finetune: 1024->2048 on 10B tokens, ->4096 on 100B, ->8192 on 100B; LR for this stage not stated

inference.samples: not stated; zero-shot single evaluation per benchmark
inference.prompting: zero-shot; RWKV-4-Raven-14B vs ChatGPT with the same prompts, then prompts re-ordered so the instruction precedes the input

other.inference benchmark: text generation time and memory on CPU (x86) and NVIDIA A100 80GB, float32, HuggingFace Transformers, all parameters counted incl. embeddings; CPU model and generation lengths not stated; values only in Fig 7, 13, 14

results.setup: 45 RWKV models over (dataset, parameters) pairs, loss vs compute

results.claim: Extrapolating the fit one order of magnitude further still fits
RWKV is on par with similarly sized Pythia, OPT and BLOOM on average zero-shot accuracy at matched FLOPs (read from plots, no numeric table)

results.quote: performs on par with similarly sized Transformers

limits: Linear attention funnels information through a single vector and may limit recall of minutiae over very long contexts (Sec 9).
Performance is more sensitive to prompt construction than for transformers; best to place the instruction before the input (Sec 9, App L).
Baselines were trained on a similar but not identical number of tokens; comparison is FLOP-matched and reported as plots, not tables.
Inference benchmarks only in float32; quantization left to future work; no numeric inference table.
No seeds, variances, GPU-hour or hardware details for pretraining; decoding settings for chat comparison not stated.
LRA: RWKV fails Path-X and trails S4 on Image and Pathfinder.
